name: Multiplicative Measure Comparison

1.definition: Expresses a ratio between quantities on a scale.

examples.form: This cabinet is [twice as deep as that one].

projection.target: Twice measures the ratio of depths rather than repetition of the cabinet state. Twice as deep fixes a ratio in a way that two centimetres deeper does not.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Saying how many times as much
curious.summary: A multiplier such as twice, followed by as and a measure word, compares two amounts as a ratio.
curious.body:
This cabinet is twice as deep as that one says that one depth is two times the other. Twice here gives a ratio between two depths. It doesn't mean the cabinet is repeated.

This is a different kind of comparison from two centimetres deeper. That version gives a difference between the depths, while twice as deep fixes how many times one is the other.

examples.text: This cabinet is [twice as deep as that one].

curious.try: Compare This cabinet is twice as deep as that one with This cabinet is two centimetres deeper than that one. Which one tells you a ratio?

teacher.summary: Useful for explaining multiplier plus as...as comparisons and how they differ from comparisons that give a difference.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a multiplier + as + a gradable expression + an as-phrase, a specialization of the equative as...as. It expresses a ratio between quantities on a scale. In twice as deep as that one, twice measures the ratio of depths, not repetition of the cabinet state. That fixes the ratio in a way that a differential such as two centimetres deeper does not: the differential gives the size of the gap, not how many times one measure is the other.
teacher.terms: Equative: a comparison of equal degree, as in as deep as. Multiplier: a word like twice that scales the comparison. Differential: a measured difference, as in two centimetres deeper.

examples.text: This cabinet is [twice as deep as that one].

contrasts.text: This cabinet is twice as deep as that one.
This cabinet is two centimetres deeper than that one.

watch_for: A learner might read twice as saying the cabinet itself occurs twice, when it states a ratio of depths.
A learner might treat twice as deep as that one as a measured difference, when it states a ratio.
teacher.activity: Give students two objects and a ruler. They measure both and say a ratio sentence (one is twice as long as the other) and a difference sentence (one is two centimetres longer).

child.hook: If one rope is twice as long as another, how long is it?
child.explain: Twice as long as means two times the length. It compares two things and tells how many times as long one is.

examples.text: This cabinet is [twice as deep as that one].
This rope is [twice as long as that one].

child.play: Find two pencils or two strings. Can you find a pair where one is twice as long as the other? Say it as a sentence.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Multiplicative Measure Comparison." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/comparative-factor-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
